newsitem.title: USA: Strong reserve levels in Ohio budget - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Strong reserve levels in Ohio budget - S&P.

text.p: Ohio Gov. George Voinovich's proposed fiscal 1998-99 biennial budget controls spending growth and continues the state's efforts at maintaining strong reserve levels, according to Standard & Poor's Corp.'s CreditWeek Municipal publication Monday.
The budget, which contains no new or increased taxes, maintains a rainy day fund reserve at five percent of annual revenues, Standard & Poor's said.

The rating agency said the $36.14 billion general fund budget "continues Ohio's record of strong fiscal management" that was verified in a July upgrade of the state's general obligation rating to AA-plus.
The rating agency also cited Ohio's continuing effort to shift Medicaid recipients into managed-care programs.
"The state has been successful in recent years in controlling areas of high growth spending and recent federal legislation should encourage continued progress," Standard & Poor's wrote.
